items.stem: The arrival of the baby boomer generation placed an immediate and measurable strain on which American institution during the 1950s?
items.stemEs: La llegada de la generación de los baby boomers impuso una presión inmediata y medible sobre cuál institución estadounidense durante los años cincuenta?

choices.text: Colleges and universities, whose enrolment the generation doubled during the early years of the decade
choices.textEs: Las universidades, cuya matrícula esta generación duplicó durante los primeros años de la década
choices.explanation: Enrolment did surge, and this generation did it — from the middle 1960s onward, when the children born in 1946 turned eighteen. Early-1950s campus growth came from veterans using the G.I. Bill, who were not boomers.
choices.misconception: credits the generation with a college surge that arrived about fifteen years later

choices.text: Public elementary schools, which had to build classrooms and hire teachers faster than at any earlier point
choices.textEs: Las escuelas primarias públicas, que tuvieron que construir aulas y contratar maestros más rápido que en cualquier momento anterior

choices.text: Social Security, whose retirement rolls the generation began to enter during the decade
choices.textEs: La Seguridad Social, cuyas listas de jubilación esta generación empezó a engrosar durante la década
choices.explanation: Social Security did grow in the 1950s, as coverage was extended to farm and domestic workers. This generation reached retirement after 2008, six decades on, and the pressure it puts on the system is a fact about our century.
choices.misconception: sends a generation of newborns onto the retirement rolls in the decade of their birth

choices.text: Veterans' hospitals, which expanded through the decade to treat the injuries the generation brought home from the war
choices.textEs: Los hospitales de veteranos, que se expandieron durante la década para atender las heridas que esta generación trajo a casa de la guerra
choices.explanation: Veterans' hospitals did expand sharply in these years, for the sixteen million Americans who had served in the Second World War. The boomers are those veterans' children; the oldest was nineteen when American ground troops entered Vietnam.
choices.misconception: treats a generation as the veterans of the war their parents fought

items.dokRationale: Recall of where a demographic surge landed first. The student matches a generation to an institution; no reasoning about why one sector responded before another is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that reasoning.
items.explanation: A birth cohort reaches institutions in the order of a human life. Children born from 1946 were five or six by the early 1950s, so elementary classrooms met the surge before any other public service did — districts ran double sessions, built on a scale not seen before, and still could not hire teachers fast enough.
items.explanationEs: Una cohorte de nacimientos llega a las instituciones en el orden de una vida humana. Los niños nacidos desde 1946 tenían cinco o seis años a comienzos de los cincuenta, de modo que las aulas de primaria enfrentaron el aumento antes que cualquier otro servicio público: los distritos organizaron doble turno, construyeron a una escala sin precedentes y aun así no pudieron contratar maestros con suficiente rapidez.

items.stem: The Levittown subdivision on Long Island sold roughly 17,400 nearly identical houses beginning in 1947. How does that development connect the baby boomer generation to the economy of the period?
items.stemEs: La urbanización Levittown, en Long Island, vendió unas 17.400 casas casi idénticas a partir de 1947. ¿Cómo conecta ese desarrollo a la generación de los baby boomers con la economía de la época?

choices.text: The houses were built for returning veterans before the birth surge began, so the two developments are unrelated
choices.textEs: Las casas se construyeron para los veteranos que regresaban antes de que comenzara el aumento de nacimientos, de modo que los dos fenómenos no están relacionados
choices.explanation: Levittown was marketed to veterans and their mortgages were guaranteed under the G.I. Bill, so the first clause is right. The two were simultaneous, not sequential: the veterans buying those houses in 1947 were the parents of the boom, and the surge was already two years old.
choices.misconception: separates two simultaneous developments by treating one as finished before the other began

choices.text: Suburban growth drew families out of the cities, which the Interstate Highway Act had already made possible
choices.textEs: El crecimiento suburbano sacó a las familias de las ciudades, lo que la Ley de Carreteras Interestatales ya había hecho posible
choices.explanation: The act is real and it did accelerate suburban growth — after 1956, nine years after these houses went up. Levittown was built along an existing commuter railway, and the highways followed the suburbs rather than preceding them.
choices.misconception: places a 1956 law before the 1947 development it is said to have enabled

choices.text: A generation of new families needed housing at once, and mass-produced subdivisions were how builders met that demand at a price buyers could reach
choices.textEs: Una generación de familias nuevas necesitaba vivienda de inmediato, y las urbanizaciones producidas en serie fueron la forma en que los constructores atendieron esa demanda a un precio alcanzable para los compradores

choices.text: The Federal Housing Administration would not insure mortgages on tract subdivisions of this kind, so buyers in places like Levittown had to find the whole purchase price in cash
choices.textEs: La Administración Federal de Vivienda no aseguraría hipotecas sobre urbanizaciones en serie de ese tipo, de modo que los compradores en lugares como Levittown tenían que reunir todo el precio de compra en efectivo
choices.explanation: The reverse is true, and it is the heart of the story: federal mortgage insurance through that administration and the Veterans Administration is what let a buyer purchase with little down and a long term, and the agencies favoured new suburban construction over older city housing.
choices.misconception: inverts the role of federal mortgage insurance in financing the suburbs

items.dokRationale: The student must reason from a construction method to the demographic demand that made it pay, and reject three statements that are each true of some part of the story. Naming Levittown as the first mass suburb is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: A birth surge is a housing problem before it is anything else. Millions of new households needed a place at once, and standardised construction on cheap outlying land was how builders met that demand at a price a federally insured mortgage could carry — so the generation's economic mark appears first as a changed landscape rather than as a changed market.
items.explanationEs: Un aumento de nacimientos es un problema de vivienda antes que cualquier otra cosa. Millones de hogares nuevos necesitaban un lugar de inmediato, y la construcción estandarizada en terrenos periféricos baratos fue la forma en que los constructores atendieron esa demanda a un precio que una hipoteca asegurada por el gobierno federal podía sostener: la huella económica de la generación aparece primero como un paisaje cambiado y no como un mercado cambiado.

items.stem: American advertisers began treating teenagers as a market worth addressing on their own in the later 1950s. What about the baby boomer generation best explains why that happened then rather than a decade earlier?
items.stemEs: Los anunciantes estadounidenses empezaron a tratar a los adolescentes como un mercado que valía la pena atender por sí mismo a finales de los años cincuenta. ¿Qué aspecto de la generación de los baby boomers explica mejor por qué eso ocurrió entonces y no una década antes?

choices.text: Its leading edge reached its teens in the later 1950s, so there were enough teenagers with spending money to be worth a separate appeal
choices.textEs: Su primera camada llegó a la adolescencia a finales de los cincuenta, de modo que había suficientes adolescentes con dinero para gastar como para merecer un mensaje aparte

choices.text: Rock and roll created the market, since Elvis Presley's first recordings appeared in 1954 and reached a national audience within two years
choices.textEs: El rock and roll creó el mercado, ya que las primeras grabaciones de Elvis Presley aparecieron en 1954 y alcanzaron un público nacional en menos de dos años
choices.explanation: Both facts are right and the music is genuinely part of the story. It arrived alongside the audience rather than producing it: a record sells to teenagers because there are a great many of them with money, and that condition is what the question is about.
choices.misconception: reads a cultural product that arrived with a market as the cause of it

choices.text: Television had only just been invented, so there had been no way to reach a young audience before this point
choices.textEs: La televisión apenas se había inventado, de modo que antes no había manera de llegar a un público joven
choices.explanation: Commercial television broadcasting began in 1941 and radio had carried programmes aimed at children since the 1930s. The medium was available well before the audience was large enough to justify addressing separately.
choices.misconception: explains a market's arrival by a technology that was already decades old

choices.text: Child labour restrictions had just been lifted, which gave teenagers wages of their own for the first time
choices.textEs: Las restricciones al trabajo infantil se acababan de levantar, lo que dio a los adolescentes salarios propios por primera vez
choices.explanation: The movement ran the other way. The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 restricted the employment of minors and was not repealed; teenage spending money in the 1950s came mostly from part-time work and from parents, in households with more to spare than their own parents had had.
choices.misconception: inverts the direction of child labour law to supply a reason for teenage income

items.dokRationale: The question asks why a change happened when it did, so the student must reason from the cohort's age in a given year to the size of a market. Recalling that teenagers became a consumer category in the 1950s is the DOK 1 version.
items.explanation: The explanation is arithmetic before it is culture. Children born in 1946 turned thirteen in 1959, and the cohorts behind them were larger still, so for the first time there were enough teenagers with money in their pockets for a separate appeal to pay for itself. Youth music and youth films followed that market; they did not create it.
items.explanationEs: La explicación es aritmética antes que cultural. Los niños nacidos en 1946 cumplieron trece años en 1959, y las cohortes siguientes eran aún mayores, de modo que por primera vez había suficientes adolescentes con dinero en el bolsillo para que un mensaje específico se pagara solo. La música y el cine juveniles siguieron a ese mercado; no lo crearon.
